content.thinking:
I'm setting up station ellipses sized by the tube's width and height in the local frame, then planning to loft the body separately from the rigid head part, with the body loft ending around the neck where it meets the head.

I need to extend the body bone list to include the neck joint, add proper stations through the neck into the head, then set up a separate head loft keyed off the head joint's position and aim direction. Working out the mirrored left/right joint pairs next...

Still laying out the body parts and legs...

Now I'm planning the remaining pieces: feet with pads and claws, the head loft with nose, jaw, eyes, ears and whiskers, cheek fur cards, tail nub, and small props like the bird, grass blade, and daisy. For the head coloring, I want to reuse the coat pattern but override it with a darker cap and lighter chin shading.

For the little bird companion, I'm settling on a blue-and-cream color scheme — sky blue body, darker blue cap and wings, cream belly, coral cheeks, orange beak and legs, with white wing bars and a tiny three-spike crest for a whimsical touch. I'm also figuring out where to position it relative to the head's top surface.

Working out the bird's body proportions...

Still defining wing geometry and axes... now moving to the tail feathers, planning three leaf-shaped extrusions fanning outward from the body's rear, angled back and slightly upward with lateral spread.

Tapering the tail feathers with a radius function and rounding the caps. Now I'm planning the bird's joint hierarchy: body, head, jaw, wings, tail, and leg joints all parented appropriately, then attaching a sphere mesh for the body.

Painting the body sphere with countershading between blue and cream, and now scattering fur cards across the body surface using a randomized distribution with distance filtering and leaning/bending parameters for a natural tufted look.

Thinking about the whimsical sculpt proportions—bigger head, chubby body, short legs—and planning simpler sphere-based eyes with dark pupils and white highlights instead of decals, positioning them using azimuth/elevation coordinates on the head surface while keeping the flat color palette under the 64-color limit.

For the eye geometry, I'm placing a small sphere partially embedded into the head surface at the hit point, offset slightly outward along the normal so it protrudes naturally, then considering a hemisphere lid aligned to world-up rather than the surface normal.

I'm noticing that if the lid covers too much of the eyeball's visible bulge, the eye would look sleepy, so I'm adjusting the eyeball to sit out further and making the lid thinner and tilted to only cover the upper portion properly.

For the whimsical touch, I'm placing a small sparkle sphere offset from the eye center along the normal and slightly upward to catch the light, planning to fine-tune its position after preview. Then I'm moving on to positioning the ears on the head.

Shaping ear outline geometry...

Writing the toes build function...

Pad bone belongs to the foot joint. Hind feet need to be bigger with three toes spaced further apart and longer than the front ones. Time to start coding this up.
